title: Universal incident fingerprint reuse, semantic root-cause prevention and agent preflight
root_cause: The existing registry, learning and auto-projection controls do not by themselves prove that every error outside repository-controlled actions is captured and consulted by every future worker. Repeated historical CI and external side-effect incidents show the importance of deterministic root-cause deduplication, next-worker discovery and evidence-bound closure.
impact: Recurring failure classes can be rediscovered as new incidents or repaired in duplicate; intermittent tool/stream interruptions may lose continuity; green may be claimed without proof.
failed_approaches: Chat-only memory or a prose status as the source of incident truth
A separate memory store/scheduler/repair PR for the same root cause
Treating green CI, dispatched posts, or historical assertions as proven end outcomes
fix: Strengthen the existing AGENTS and Powerhouse Continuity skill with mandatory fingerprint-first incident preflight, semantic deduplication, durable incident evidence, bounded same-lineage recovery and fail-closed proof semantics. Add a regression contract guarding these requirements.
prevention_rule: Before any material work every agent/chat must load known failure fingerprints and derived skills, deduplicate by semantic root cause, update the same canonical incident/occurrence and remediation owner, add a real regression and only mark PROVEN after exact-head/provider/outcome/learning-skill-readback. A context/tool interruption resumes the existing obligation with no duplicate side effects.
outcome: CANDIDATE. Governance/test/learning changes proposed; CI, merge, skill projection, production and next-worker discovery remain unverified until external readback.
